You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Each panel uses two colors, with exactly one color shared between both panels. Output is the cellwise agreement mask for the shared color: dimensions equal one panel; fill output with the shared color, except output 3 wherever the aligned cell in BOTH panels is that shared color. Compare aligned coordinates directly; do not reverse/flip panels; exclude divider.

Evidence from demos: horizontal demo 1 had divider color 4, upper palette {1,5}, lower palette {2,5}; shared color=5, output 9x21 filled with 5 and 3 exactly where both corresponding cells were 5. The task is robust to divider orientation and differing panel-specific colors. The input is partitioned by full-width/full-height separator lines into equal rectangular panels; output has one cell per panel in the same layout. Count the scattered marker-color cells in each panel: in observed instances, panels with exactly one marker map to the original background color, while panels with exactly two markers map to color 1. Ignore separator lines and preserve panel ordering (row-major). Demo 1: input 17x11, background 8, marker 6, separators 7; 3x3 panels of size 5x3. General approach: identify row/column dividers, partition into panels, count marker cells per panel, and emit a compressed grid with original background for singletons and 1 for panels containing two markers.
